title: Russian famine of 1891–1892
summary: The English Wikipedia article "Russian famine of 1891–1892", at revision 1380469146, opens: "The 1891–1892 famine in the Russian Empire, sometimes called the Tsar Famine, Tsar's Famine or Black Earth Famine, began along the Volga River and spread as far as the Urals and the Black Sea. This area included the provinces of Nizhni-Novgorod, Ryazan, Tula, Kazan, Simbirsk, Saratov, Penza, Samara and Tambov. The famine was initially caused by poor weather and was exacerbated by poor logistical networks, and a lack of grain reserves due to the Russian government's export policy." That is the article's account and not yet this atlas's; nobody has read this record, and review.html is where somebody does. Wikidata item Q3066272, imported by tools/import/wikidata.mjs. The item's own description reads "Imperial Russian famine and epidemic". Everything here is copied from the item's own fields and nothing in it is this atlas's account of the thing: that is still to be written, and review.html is where somebody writes it.
